The Story of Nagdatta

I bow to Lord Jina, worshipped by gods, Vidyadharas, Chakravartins, kings, and maharajas, and I write the story of Nagdatta.

In the city of Nasakya in the land of Abhir, there lived a merchant named Sagardatt. His wife was Nagdatta. They had a son and a daughter named Shrikumar and Shrishena. Nagdatta's conduct was not good. She had an illicit affair with a cowherd named Nand. One day she instigated him, and he pretended to be sick and did not come to graze the cows. Poor Sagardatt had to go himself. In the forest, he left the cows grazing and fell asleep under a tree. Nand came and killed him. Nagdatta had incited him to murder her husband. And what wicked deed will a lustful man not commit to remove obstacles to his pleasure?

Nagdatta and the sinful Nand, having loaded a great burden of sin upon their heads through this atrocity, began to enjoy their base desires. Shrikumar was deeply distressed by his mother's wickedness. He found it hard to show his face to anyone. He felt great shame and scolded his mother severely. But Nagdatta was unmoved. Like a bitten snake, she turned her venom upon him. She incited Nand to kill Shrikumar as well.

Nand again pretended to be sick and did not come to graze the cows. Shrikumar prepared to go himself. His sister Shrishena stopped him and said, "Brother, do not go. I see some deceit in mother's plan. Just as she had father killed through Nand, she is now plotting to have you killed too. That is why Nand is pretending to be sick today."

Shrikumar said, "Sister, you have warned me well today. Do not worry. I can protect myself. I am not afraid at all. And I am not going because you asked me to — but if I refuse to go, mother will become more suspicious and devise some other plan to have me killed, for she never sits quiet."

So Shrikumar went to the forest, but he was prepared. He carried weapons and kept his wits about him. When Nand attacked him, Shrikumar fought back and killed the cowherd in self-defence. He then returned home and confronted his mother. Nagdatta, seeing her plot fail and her lover dead, was consumed by rage and grief. She eventually perished miserably, reaping the fruit of her sins.

Shrikumar and Shrishena, having witnessed the terrible consequences of their mother's adultery and murder, became deeply detached from worldly life. They renounced everything, became monks, and through dedicated spiritual practice, attained liberation.

This story teaches that adultery and murder are among the gravest sins, and those who commit them bring destruction upon themselves and all around them. Nagdatta's wickedness led to the death of her husband, her lover, and ultimately herself. But her children, through wisdom and detachment, escaped her poison and found the path to liberation.
